entries.action: Constrain R-BODY-2 to FIXED UNIFORM patches (len 8/16, stride 4/8 as specced): never add adaptive routing, semantic graphs, or dynamic boundaries. Any future adaptive-patch proposal must first beat the tuned uniform baseline in-probe.
entries.note: bitrate-allocation theory + isolation study on 3 architectures: without coupling constraints local complexity cannot justify non-uniform optima; validation-selected uniform patch is competitive with dynamic patching (effects ~0, no consistent direction); gains are method/dataset-specific. Adaptive patching must be evaluated against a tuned uniform baseline.
entries.title: Adaptive Patching Is Harder Than It Looks For Time-Series Forecasting

entries.action: Two R-BODY-2 refinements: (a) prioritize WIDTH over patch-grouping cleverness; (b) keep the frozen-body + train-readout pattern (our B3 instrument) — fitting a frozen parent's trajectory is easier than fitting the future directly.
entries.note: atomic-encoding study: more sensitivity to model width than atom grouping. Frozen parent recursive trajectory easier to fit than observed future; Autoregressive Trajectory Distillation gives selectable ATD-1/2/4/8 execution (ATD-1 = parent exactly), 5.54x speedup at stable quality.
entries.relevance: R-BODY-2 design priorities + frozen-body pattern support.
entries.title: One Patch, Three Roles: What Is Actually Coupled in Autoregressive Time-Series Forecasting?

entries.action: Channel-design rule for R-BODY-1/2: neither pure channel-independent nor fully channel-dependent — route per patch by spectral energy (low/mid/high bands) with frequency-specific experts. Our 10-indicator set has exactly the smooth-trend + local-fluctuation + abrupt-transition mix this addresses.
entries.note: generic plugin balancing CI/CD per patch via graph spectral decomposition: shared graph Fourier basis, patches grouped by spectral energy, channel-adaptive routing adjusts inter-channel interaction per patch. Improves both accuracy and generalization on top of existing CI and CD models. Accepted ICLR 2026.
entries.title: Routing Channel-Patch Dependencies in Time Series Forecasting with Graph Spectral Decomposition

entries.action: Regime-direction for memory/evolution work: adaptive regime detection + continual accumulate-and-transfer across regimes (not rolling retrain, not naive online fine-tune). Resonates with our regime-memory ideas (RG-TTA gate, RACE gate) and frames any future memory-revisit as a continual-learning problem.
entries.note: ReCAP: adaptive regime detection + continual learning for portfolio management; rolling retraining costs too much, naive online fine-tuning utilizes too little; accumulate and transfer knowledge across sequential regime-tasks.
entries.relevance: Memory/evolution regime direction (dormant until P1 family passes).
entries.title: Regime-Adaptive Continual Learning for Portfolio Management

entries.action: R-BODY-2 per-window note: dominant periods vary by window, not just dataset — identify cycles per input window and refine early patches with broader context while preserving near-boundary patches. De-cycled residual needs multi-resolution handling.
entries.note: CAMP: per-window adaptive cycle learning (no preset cycle length) + horizon-guided position-dependent patch mixer + multi-resolution de-cycled residual; best avg MSE on 6/7 long-term benchmarks, best/tied MAE on 6.
entries.title: CAMP: A Cycle-Aware Multi-Scale Patch Mixer for Time Series Forecasting
